hook: The email record that ties checks to the address you see.
definition: A DNS record that ties SPF and DKIM checks to the From address. It passes only when one of them passes for that domain.
example: MailRoute says Outlook.com rejected some mail from domains without DMARC on Nov 5–9, then Microsoft rolled back a spam-rule update it blamed.
the_catch: A DMARC record alone does not make mail pass. Without aligned SPF or DKIM it fails, and p=none asks receivers to take no action.
caption: DMARC is the DNS record that ties SPF and DKIM checks to the From address, and a record alone won't help without an aligned check. Have you ever had an email bounce for no clear reason?
alt_text: A five-slide glossary carousel defining DMARC: a DNS record that ties SPF and DKIM checks to the From address, an example from an earlier gummietech post about Outlook.com rejecting some mail, and the common mistake of thinking a record alone makes mail pass.

es.hook: El registro de correo electrónico que vincula las verificaciones a la dirección que ves
es.definition: Un registro DNS que vincula las verificaciones SPF y DKIM con la dirección From. Solo se aprueba cuando una de ellas pasa para ese dominio
es.example: MailRoute indica que Outlook.com rechazó algunos correos de dominios sin DMARC del 5 al 9 de noviembre, y luego Microsoft revocó una actualización de regla antispam que había señalado como causa
es.the_catch: Un registro DMARC por sí solo no hace que el correo pase. Sin SPF o DKIM alineados, falla, y p=none indica a los receptores que no tomen ninguna medida
